deployment_decision.reason: One consistent lost success and no gains on the fresh holdout; slower total capped workload. No retuning after holdout.

metadata.protocol: Existing 48-tree portfolio corpus, explicitly development data. Compare missing-count and missing-sum swap objectives without exact fallback, each with 40000 proposals and min(0.1s, 10% of the configured attempt allowance). Alternate objective order. Seed and corpus are fixed; wall cutoffs may vary. Choose an objective and freeze the algorithm before running the separate fresh holdout. Scores from the two objectives have different scales and are not compared numerically across objectives. The fixed proposal policy is missing_difference; missing_difference uses a 3:1 targeted/uniform proposal mixture, while uniform samples vertex pairs uniformly. The policy is selected before this archive's measurements.

metadata.protocol: 48 unique non-caterpillar trees: six per family/order at 35 and 75 vertices; excludes every class in all four earlier benchmark corpora. Inputs, objective and method limits are frozen before timing. No tuning after holdout results. Every route uses the same exact CP-SAT fallback and complete attempt wall allowance; candidates get min(0.1s, 10% of that allowance). The portfolio reserves half its candidate time for v3, then gives remaining time to swaps. Baseline and swaps each have a 40000-operation cap; portfolio has 40000 frontier nodes plus 40000 swap proposals. These operations are different and the comparison is equal-time, not equal-work. Method order rotates. Timings measure the whole solve() call, including candidate search and exact-model preparation; archive writing outside solve() and the independent benchmark witness check are excluded. All fallback hashes must match an independently built original model. The fixed proposal policy is missing_difference; missing_difference uses a 3:1 targeted/uniform proposal mixture, while uniform samples vertex pairs uniformly. The policy is selected before this archive's measurements.
